title: Tip a rocker so its counterweight can pass the stop, then leave it resting on the new stop
instruction: Tip the rocker beam over so its left end rests on the green stop; while it is tipped, turn the orange counterweight round to the yellow mark. Let go of both handles and leave the rocker resting on the green stop.
context: Pivoted inspection fixtures (rockers, balance beams, tilt arms) are rebalanced by moving an eccentric counterweight past a fixed obstacle without removing it. The obstacle blocks the weight at the fixture's rest angle, so a technician tips the fixture with one hand, holds it, turns the weight with the other, and lets both go so the fixture settles on its other stop. Letting go too early drops the fixture back and can trap fingers.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Rocker centred at (0.30, 0.00). Fixed base (grey): a 9 x 12 cm plate, 6 mm thick, and a 4 x 3 cm pedestal 2.6 cm tall. The beam (grey, 4 x 34 cm, 1.6 cm thick, 60 g bar) rotates about an 8 mm axle along x at 4.2 cm height, through the middle of the pedestal. Its angle runs from +8 degrees (right end down, the start) to -8 degrees (left end down), limited by a red rubber stop under the right end and a green one under the left end (each 4 x 10 cm, 1.1 cm tall, centred at y = -0.15 and +0.15). Left end: a dark steel ballast block (4 x 4 x 2 cm, 200 g) centred at y = +0.15 on the beam, with a blue round handle (3.2 cm diameter, 4 cm tall, 20 g) on top. Near the right end: a white turntable (7 cm diameter, 6 mm thick, 20 g) on a vertical axis at y = -0.15; on it an orange counterweight (200 g in all): a 6 cm arm carrying a 3 x 3 x 2.5 cm block (150 g) centred 5 cm from the axis, and an orange round handle (3.2 cm diameter, 4 cm tall, 30 g) on the block. The turntable has friction (the weight stays where it is put), turns from -10 to 190 degrees only, and starts with the weight turned out toward the right end (block at y = -0.20, x = 0.30). Turning it through the front (toward +x) takes the block round to y = -0.10, over the yellow mark (a 3.4 x 3 cm patch on the beam top at y = -0.085 to -0.055). A dark post (2 cm diameter, 5.7 cm tall) stands at (0.35, -0.148): on the red stop the weight's bottom is 2.2 cm below the post top and level it is about level with it, so the weight cannot pass; with the beam on the green stop the weight's bottom is 2.0 cm above the post top. The beam is balanced with the weight at the front: weight turned out it is right-heavy (0.093 N m), turned in it is left-heavy (0.093 N m). Pivot damping 0.08 N m s/rad, no friction. The handles are about 0.35 m apart at the start and 0.25 m at the end.
scoring: 0 if the counterweight is forced through the post (its bottom more than 6 mm below the post top while it is between 55 and 125 degrees round). Otherwise, at the end: 0.25 once the beam has been tipped far enough for the weight to clear the post by 8 mm (at any time); 0.5 once the weight has then been swung past 100 degrees (at any time); 0.75 while the weight is within 8 degrees of the yellow mark (180 degrees round) and the beam is within 5 degrees of the green stop (its angle -8 degrees), but a gripper is still within 6 cm of a handle, the beam or the weight block (or the beam is still moving). Success (1.0, held 2 s): that pose, the beam at rest (under 8 degrees per second), no gripper within 6 cm of a handle, the beam or the weight block (a gripper counts as holding within 4.5 cm with its fingers less than 6.5 cm apart), and no violation. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0.
reset_notes: Turn the counterweight round to the right (out toward the right end, until it stops at its pin, block at y = -0.20), then let the beam settle on the red stop (right end down, +8 degrees). Check the post stands upright at (0.35, -0.148) and that the weight turns by hand without slipping when the beam is tipped.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Both pivots are real revolute joints in the engine; the stops are the beam joint's limits, drawn as coloured blocks. Beam pivot: damping 0.08 N m s/rad, no friction. Turntable: PhysX joint friction 0.3, damping 0.01, a tuned value rather than a measured one. Mass, centre of mass and inertia come from the parts. The score reads the two joint angles and the arms' tool points; the zero gate is geometric (weight bottom against the post top).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the arms reached the handles but the rocker never reached the target pose); demo: 1.0
